production.note: US model year 2010 only, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): the 2010 Murciélago lists "LP 670-4 SuperVeloce Coupe 2D". The existing LP 640 record found that KBB's 2011 Murciélago address returns the 2010 page and the Aventador replaced it for 2012. Lamborghini's release (Geneva, March 2009): "limited to just 350 units".

aspiration.note: Naturally aspirated V12 per the release

drivetrain.note: "Permanent all-wheel drive with Viscous Traction system"

transmission.note: "Gearbox 6-speed e-gear" as standard; "As a no-premium option, the SuperVeloce is available with a six-speed manual transmission." (e-gear is a single-clutch automated manual)

powerHp.note: Quote (Lamborghini release and technical data, reproduced in full by AutoGuide): "Maximum power 670 hp (493 kW) at 8000 rpm". The 670 is Lamborghini's metric (CV/PS) figure: 670 x 0.98632 = 661 hp. Evo's spec table agrees: "661bhp @ 8000rpm" (evo-murcielago). No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (step 4): no curb weight for the standard car, and no optioned-car curb weight, was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine. Quote (Lamborghini technical data): "Dry weight 1565 Kg. (3450.2 lb)". 1,565 x 2.20462 = 3,450 lb. Evo's table agrees: "1565kg (dry) (429bhp/ton)" (evo-murcielago). The release does not say whether this is with options.
